sections.html:
Utah Valley's northern end is where Lehi lies, in Utah County. The city stayed small for a century, with a census low of 2,733 in 1940 and only 8,475 in 1990, then took off: 19,028 in 2000, 47,407 in 2010 and 75,907 in 2020, with an estimate of 95,313 for July 2025. Median age in 2020 was 26.2, and roughly 39.5 percent of residents were minors.

Most homes are sized for families. A house in the old town grid looks nothing like a recent subdivision, and buyers compare them on age and condition.

Many owners here bought during a tech hiring wave. A layoff, a remote work shift or a job offer elsewhere can force a move, and the main challenge then is timing, since the mortgage payment continues while the house waits for a buyer.

Interstate 15 runs through Lehi with five exits, and commuters count that among the city's best selling points. FrontRunner commuter rail opened its Lehi station near Thanksgiving Point on December 12, 2012, and Utah Transit Authority runs local buses. A buyer's agent will price in distance to an I-15 ramp or the station, so a house far from the interstate may draw a different buyer than one close to the Corporate Center on Traverse Mountain.

sections.h2: Schools and the coming district split
sections.html: Lehi public schools, including Lehi High and Skyridge High, have been run by the Alpine School District. The Alpine district ends in July 2027, and three new districts, including one named Aspen Peaks, take its place. Before you tell a buyer anything about schools, ask the district or the city which one will cover the exact property.

All building permits come from the Building and Inspections Department, and unfinished work under an open permit can delay a closing. Applications are filed through an online portal, and the codes now in force include the 2021 I-Codes and the 2020 National Electrical Code with Utah amendments.

  • Book an inspection by calling 385-201-1035 a full day ahead. Voicemail, email and online requests do not book one.
  • Have the work ready first, because re-inspection fees apply when a project clearly is not.
  • Look up status by permit number, site address or subdivision and lot.

Lehi City is at 131 N 100 E, phone (385) 201-1000.

Lehi runs a pressurized irrigation system that supplies untreated water for yards and city fire hydrants. A city ordinance prohibits irrigation water use after October 15, owners turn the connection on and off each year, and the city is currently in Phase 2 of its Water Shortage Management Plan. Buyers from elsewhere often ask how the yard is watered, so explain the connection and watering schedule up front.

sections.h2: Valuation notices, tax bills and recording
sections.html:
In Utah County, valuation notices come in summer, tax notices in October, and payment is expected by 5:00 pm on November 30. To appeal, go through the Auditor at 111 S. University Ave, Provo, or phone (801) 851-8109, option 3, and the Board of Equalization will hear it. September 15 is the usual deadline, though the date on your own notice rules.

A valuation notice is no bill. What you owe shows up in the October tax notice, so if you close in the fall, ask the title company how that year's taxes are being split.

The Utah County Recorder files deeds, historically for $40 per document. Fees change, so get the current amount from the recorder before closing.

sections.h2: Does the primary residence exemption follow the house?
sections.html:
It stays with the owner, not the house. A primary home is taxed on 55 percent of market value because Utah takes off 45 percent, provided the owner lives there at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year.

A buyer needs to file Form TC-473A with the county Board of Equalization by September 15 after a sale or deed transfer, and late filings are refused. Miss it and the new owner may owe tax on full market value that year. Rental owners file a residential declaration signed by every owner, and second or vacation homes do not qualify.

Warn your buyer about the deadline early so a fall closing does not end in a surprise bill.

sections.h2: Selling with open permits or liens
sections.html:
Permits left open cause the most trouble in a fast closing. Suppose a basement, deck or remodel never passed its final inspection: a lender may want it closed out, and that starts with a call to 385-201-1035 and a day of notice. A cash buyer can often take the house as it stands, yet the item still appears in the paperwork, so learn what is open before you sign.

Liens get settled at closing. The title search turns up unpaid taxes, a mortgage payoff or a judgment against the property, and each is paid from your proceeds before you get the balance. Ask for the figures before signing day.

sections.h2: What to gather before you call
sections.html: Start with the deed, the newest tax notice, permit records for finished space and a recent mortgage statement. Jot down when the irrigation connection gets switched on each year. For an estate sale, include the court papers naming who may sign. Armed with all of it, a buyer can price the house in one conversation and the title company can begin searching at once.

sections.h2: Choosing between listing and a direct sale
sections.html: A regular listing in Lehi means cleaning, repairs and showings, then waiting through a buyer's inspection and loan approval. That can work well for a house in good shape with time to spare. A direct sale fits better when the clock is short, the house needs work, or the owner is dealing with a job change, an estate or missed payments. Compare what a listing would net after repairs, commission and months of mortgage payments against a direct offer, and ask any buyer for proof of funds in writing.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works for a Lehi house
sections.html:
Title and recording work the same way in a cash sale, minus lender approval. A title company hunts for liens, everyone signs, and the deed is recorded in Provo.

  1. Describe the house, its condition and your timeline.
  2. Set the offer and closing date beside a listing plan.
  3. Resolve open permits or liens before the closing date.
  4. Sign, then collect proceeds after payoffs and prorated taxes.

That path suits owners who inherited a Lehi house, are behind on payments, or have a house that needs work they do not want to finance. There are no showings and no repair negotiations, and the closing date is set with you. You also skip the wait for a buyer's loan, which in a fast-moving market is often the step that falls through late.

faqs.q: How many people live in Lehi, Utah?
faqs.a: About 95,313 as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 75,907, up from 47,407 in 2010.

faqs.q: When are Utah County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By 5:00 pm on November 30. Utah County mails tax notices in October, and a valuation notice is not a bill.

faqs.q: What is the Utah County appeal deadline for a Lehi property valuation?
faqs.a: September 15 in a typical year. Check the notice you receive, since the date printed on it governs.

faqs.q: Will Alpine School District still serve Lehi?
faqs.a: Not after July 2027. Alpine School District will be replaced by three new districts, so confirm the district for a specific address before telling buyers.

faqs.q: Who inspects building work in Lehi?
faqs.a: The city's Building and Inspections Department. Call 385-201-1035 at least 24 hours ahead to schedule an inspection.
